ecological_anchor.reference: Dellinger et al. 2026, American Journal of Botany, DOI 10.1002/ajb2.70044
ecological_anchor.rationale: The published macroecological analysis associates pink/red flowers with cold conditions and purple/yellow flowers with aridity and/or UV-B. If these colors repeatedly arise under abiotic selection in distant lineages, they should retain less clade-internal phylogenetic memory than white.

relative_time_axis: pairwise patristic distance / (2 * source-tree crown height); require root-to-tip CV <= 1e-8

focal_color_memory.sampling_unit: directed focal-color species -> every other retained species
focal_color_memory.baseline: (k-1)/(n-1), where k is focal-color tip count
focal_color_memory.binning: equal directed-pair count by relative divergence depth
focal_color_memory.primary_color_metric: signed trapezoid area of focal-color excess-retention curve

clade_contrast.stress_metric: mean signed area across eligible stress-associated colors present in that clade

primary_test.prediction: stress-associated colors have weaker phylogenetic memory than white
primary_test.statistic: paired one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test across clades
primary_test.pass_rule: median contrast < 0 and one-sided Wilcoxon P <= 0.05

secondary_diagnostics: individual pink/red/purple/yellow versus white paired contrasts
claim_boundary: retrospective derived test on already-opened flower-color outcomes
environment-color associations come from Dellinger et al. 2026 and are not re-estimated here
a PASS is consistent with repeated ecological convergence but does not establish abiotic causation
a FAIL rejects this simple stress-color convergence prediction without rejecting environment-color associations themselves
